version.approval_notes: Kits Editor for Firefox restyles Firefox's own interface (tab bar, toolbar, address bar), which extensions can't do directly, so it uses userChrome.css through a native messaging helper (native-host/ in the source repo; Python standard library only) that the user installs with native-host/install.sh or install.ps1. When the user presses Apply on the settings page, the helper writes the generated stylesheet to <profile>/chrome/ and an allowlisted set of prefs to user.js, both listed on the settings page beforehand. Rules already in userChrome.css are moved to userChrome.css.ahtb-backup (they would override the stylesheet); Remove from Firefox puts them back. The prefs leave user.js once Firefox has saved them, so they apply once. To test: 1) curl -fsSL https://github.com/mattsaund/Kits-Editor-for-Firefox/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh  2) open the settings page (toolbar button), choose a layout, press Apply  3) restart Firefox. Optional permissions: technicalAndInteraction gates a twice-daily request to api.github.com for the latest release (nothing about the user is sent). <all_urls> is requested only when the user switches on "Let clicks through to the page": content/click-through.js (all frames) checks whether the element under the pointer near a window edge is clickable; copies in subframes only report the pointer position and the clickable element's box, which the background script forwards to the top frame's copy (tabs.sendMessage, frameId 0). The background script shows or hides the add-on's page action on that tab, which the stylesheet reads as a per-tab flag (the icon itself is hidden). It also runs an empty function in the active tab with scripting.executeScript; if Firefox refuses (another extension's page, about: pages), a differently titled page action shrinks the hover zones near the window corners. No page content is stored or sent; switching the option off removes the permission and the script. "management" is requested only when the user switches on "Show my themes": it lists installed themes (management.getAll, type "theme") and switches theme (management.setEnabled), also when a saved profile records one; other add-ons are never listed, changed or reported. Profiles stay in storage.local. The helper's "fonts" command lists installed font family names (fc-list on Linux; the name tables of font files in the system and user font folders on macOS and Windows) for the settings page's font list; the chosen name goes into the stylesheet as an escaped CSS string, and nothing about fonts is sent anywhere. Full source: https://github.com/mattsaund/Kits-Editor-for-Firefox
